title: zig build test-integration: non-deterministic advisory-lock contention/hangs in the test-integration-others-internal barrier group cause cascading test failures (recurrence of ISS-0106/ISS-0107/ISS-0151 class)
scope: tests/integration/** (test-integration-others-internal barrier group) — test infrastructure, not confirmed to be a production defect.
symptom: `zig build test-integration` (run against a freshly-verified-healthy BPM_TEST_DB_URL, per zig build test-env-verify HEALTHY — 10 checks passed immediately before each run) is non-deterministic and fails differently across consecutive clean runs on the SAME commit (origin/main 2c7046e1): Run 1 — 52 distinct test failures across ~30 files, nearly all sharing the signature `runMigrations failed: error.ServerError` from `vendor/pg/pg.zig:329 readUntilReady` while acquiring `pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('bpm_test_migrations_public'))` in `tests/integration/helpers.zig`, plus several `error: test runner failed to respond for ~1m<N>ms` entries and one genuine DebugAllocator leak in `sim01_04_simulation_mode_test.zig`. After restarting the db_test container and re-verifying `zig build test-env-verify` HEALTHY (0 ungranted locks), Run 2 on the identical commit produced only 2 failures, both `error: test runner failed to respond for ~1m<N>ms` against different binaries than Run 1. After Run 2, `zig build test-env-verify` again reported C6 FAIL (8 ungranted locks) until db_test was restarted again — i.e. every observed run leaves the DB in a state with stale/ungranted advisory locks afterward, regardless of how many individual test failures occurred.
reproduction: Two independent, clean `zig build test-integration --summary all` runs on origin/main @ 2c7046e1, each preceded by a verified-HEALTHY `zig build test-env-verify` (10/10 checks, 0 ungranted locks) and, for run 2, a fresh `docker compose restart db_test`. Both runs used the same BPM_TEST_DB_URL (postgres://bpm:***@localhost:5434/bpm_test, container r-co-db_test-1). No 'Build Summary: N/N steps succeeded' line was ever reached in either run — both runs end in a cascade of 'failed command' / 'error: test runner failed to respond' entries for the test-integration-others-internal barrier step, consistent with ISS-0107's documented mechanism (independent binaries in that barrier group racing/deadlocking against each other under full concurrency), not with any single deterministic assertion failure.
root_cause_analysis: Confirmed to be the SAME mechanism as ISS-0665 (RESOLVED 2026-08-12T03:59:12Z, GH #702), not a new mechanism: docker logs r-co-db_test-1 during Run 1 shows repeated "canceling statement due to statement timeout" errors clustered at ~65s intervals, exactly ISS-0665's documented symptom. ISS-0665's fix (tests/integration/helpers.zig runMigrations/runMigrationsForSchema bracketing DDL with BPM_TEST_STMT_TIMEOUT, default 300s) IS present in the current main tree (verified: lines 132-145, 210-223). BPM_TEST_STMT_TIMEOUT was not set explicitly for either evidence run, so the 300s default was active throughout, yet statement-timeout cancellations still occurred. A third run at reduced build-step concurrency (-j4, ISS-0665's other documented workaround) reduced failures from 52 (full concurrency) to 2 -- still not clean, but a strong concurrency-correlated gradient (52 -> 2 -> 2 across full/-j4/-j4-repeat) consistent with host-capacity contention rather than a deterministic code regression, matching ISS-0665's own prevention note verbatim: "a single full-concurrency zig build test-integration run reporting failures is not sufficient evidence of a real regression." CONCLUSION: this is not a new defect -- it is evidence that ISS-0665's fix (widening the DDL-window timeout to 300s) reduces but does not eliminate contention failures on this host at full concurrency, and does not fully eliminate them even at -j4. Reclassifying from "regression of the ISS-0106/0107/0151 class" to "continuation of ISS-0665, not fully resolved by its fix." Not diagnosed further per TEST-RUNNER role boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Root-cause diagnosis identifying why pg_advisory_lock('bpm_test_migrations_public') acquisition intermittently stalls/fails across the test-integration-others-internal barrier group on current main (ISSUE-FIXER)
5 consecutive clean `zig build test-integration` runs on the fix branch complete with a 'Build Summary: N/N steps succeeded' line and zero ServerError/'test runner failed to respond' entries
zig build test-env-verify reports 0 ungranted locks (C6 PASS) immediately after each of those 5 runs, with no manual db_test restart between them

sim01_04_simulation_mode_test.zig's TC-SIM-01-01 DebugAllocator leak (src/event_store/store.zig:1368 duplicateFromParams -> src/event_store/store.zig:893 append) is triaged separately — confirm whether it is a genuine allocator leak independent of the lock-contention cascade, or a symptom of the same root cause
evidence_file: Run 1 full log (1544 lines) and Run 2 full log (47 lines) captured to $TEMP during WF02-batch-6-20260812 Step 00a; not committed (raw logs, not a permanent artefact per File Placement Rules). Key run 1 failure list (52 entries) begins with gh512_t010_regression_test TC-RG-01/TC-RG-02, iss0607_pg_stderr_suppression_test, iss0123_regression_test TC-ISS-0123-02, iss208_task_guard_test TC1/TC2, and continues through env01_test/env03_test/sim01_04_simulation_mode_test — full list available on request from the TEST-RUNNER handoff for this run (handoffs/WF02-batch-6-20260812/step-00a-test-runner.json).
notes: Discovered as part of the WF02-batch-6-20260812 Green-Main Gate (Step 00a), run from a git worktree (not the primary checkout) that required first-time setup: no .env existed (copied from the primary checkout's .env, pointing at the same shared r-co Docker Compose project), and an initial `./make.ps1 up` run before docker-compose.override.yml was also copied into the worktree briefly remapped db/db_test to the unmapped default ports 5432/5433 (colliding with unrelated host processes) before being corrected — see the same run's handoff for the full timeline. This was corrected and verified (zig build test-env-verify HEALTHY, matching ports/COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME confirmed against the primary checkout) before either test-integration run captured as evidence here, and both runs' db/db_test containers were confirmed healthy on the correct ports (5442/5434) throughout — but is noted in case it is relevant to why contention was observed (e.g. residual connection-pool state from the container recreate). A machine-wide User-scope environment variable BPM_TEST_DB_URL (pointing at an unrelated checkout's port 5453) also had to be overridden per-invocation throughout this run; unrelated to this issue's mechanism (confirmed via zig build test-env-verify's C0 check resolving the correct 5434 URL in both evidence runs) but noted for whoever picks this up, since raw `zig build` invocations (not routed through make.ps1's Import-DotEnv) will silently pick up the wrong BPM_TEST_DB_URL on this host unless overridden explicitly. ADDENDUM (2026-08-12T18:49:54Z): a 4th attempted run at default concurrency, given extra time, never reached a Build Summary line either — its own process tree (confirmed via Get-Process/taskkill, not exit-code reporting) was still actively executing 11-12 concurrent test.exe binaries several minutes in, consistent with severe throughput degradation under contention rather than a quick deterministic failure. This session also observed that its own background-task completion notifications were unreliable for this exact command shape (zig.exe -> build.exe -> test.exe process tree): notifications reported completion while taskkill later proved the tree was still alive with active children on at least two separate occasions. That tooling caveat is noted for whoever picks this up but does not change the underlying finding, which rests on directly-observed Postgres server log entries (docker logs) and pg_stat_activity state, not on any zig exit code.
